text:
Tess: Quick async — posting a short status so people can pick up items. Focus: microbatch adapter, kernel perf regressions, and KV cache TTL/eviction tuning. No meeting, just updates and ownership clarifications.

Omar: Thanks. TL;DR from me: microbatch adapter PR landed in draft, needs perf tests + a small change to batch_window logic. I can own the PR finalization if someone else takes the canary.

Ben: I can take the canary deployment and watch the hotpath metrics. Which cluster? staging-3 or canary-llama?

Tess: Use canary-llama for latency-sensitive tests. staging-3 for stress tests. Omar, what's the PR number?

Omar: PR #4578. Main change: switch from fixed batch_window_ms=12 to adaptive backoff based on inflight tokens. Patch is tiny:

```
# pseudo-config
batch_window_ms: adaptive
batch_window_min_ms: 6
batch_window_max_ms: 25
backoff_alpha: 0.6
```

Omar: Tests pass locally but microbench on prod-seed shows a small increase in p99 for short sequences ~2-3ms. Need kernel owners to eyeball kernel scheduling.

Li-Wei: I saw that regression on the telemetry dashboard earlier. Looks correlated with sequence length distribution shifting to 32 tokens. Kernel scheduling is doing more context-switching for tiny batches.

Ben: I can observe traces during canary, but real fix probably in the scheduler heuristics. Who owns that?

Tess: Scheduler heuristics is owned by Ben and Li-Wei (per the ownership doc). Ben, lead the canary. Li-Wei, can you triage scheduler traces after the canary?

Li-Wei: Yep — I'll capture flamegraphs and KV cache hits. Also want to try bumping batch_window_min_ms to 8 and re-run microbench. If p99 improves we can roll with conservative default.

Ciara: FYI infra has a 30-minute maintenance window on canary-llama at 16:30 PDT tomorrow. If canary overlaps that, request a 1-hour shift.

Ben: Noted. I'll schedule the canary for 18:00 PDT to avoid the window. Will post exact time and rollout steps.

Omar: One more ask: there's a small KV-cache TTL change I included in the PR (reduce default TTL from 5m to 2m for prefix caches). Impact unknown on cache hit ratio. Can we monitor hit/miss ratio during canary?

Tess: Yes — add a dashboard panel for kv_prefix_hit_ratio and kv_eviction_rate. Use thresholds to auto-alert: kv_prefix_hit_ratio < 0.7 or kv_eviction_rate > 400/s.

Ben: I'll add the dashboard and set temporary alerting to the runtime-alerts channel. Also will attach the canary runbook with rollback steps.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled by Ben at 2024-05-14T18:00:00Z to canary-llama. Changes: PR #4578, KV TTL 5m->2m, adaptive batch window enabled. Monitoring hooks: latency, kv_hit_ratio, p99_traces.

Li-Wei: Action items I have: 1) run microbench with batch_window_min_ms=8, 2) capture flamegraphs during canary, 3) evaluate KV hit ratio delta. I'll post results here within 3 hours after canary completes.

Omar: Action items I have: 1) finish PR cleanup + tests, 2) respond to kernel review comments (cc @Ben for traces), 3) post a short summary after merge.

Ben: Action items I have: 1) run canary at 18:00 PDT and watch runtime-alerts, 2) create dashboard panels + alerts, 3) if p99 regress > 5ms rollback immediately and ping infra.

Ciara: I'll update the infra calendar and confirm the maintenance window shift if needed.

Tess: Thanks all. If anyone needs to reassign ownership ping me directly. We'll reconvene async here — share screenshots or small logs (paste a few lines) rather than big outputs. :thumbsup: 

Omar: One last note — tagging a reviewer: @Li-Wei please look at the scheduler comment in PR #4578, it's a 3-line change.

Li-Wei: Will do.

Ben: Got it. 18:00 PDT. I'll post canary link + dashboard when live.
